segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Katrin and we've got an upper intermediate level lesson for you guys today.
segments.zh: 我的名字是卡特琳，我们今天为你们准备了一节中高级课程。

segments.en: This one is all about a crime scene.
segments.zh: 这一切都是关于犯罪现场的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So we are going to be at a crime scene.
segments.zh: 所以我们将在犯罪现场。

segments.en: We are with the police officers and we're going to take a look at some very, very interesting and specific vocab to like police and a crime and all that.
segments.zh: 我们和警察在一起，我们会看一些非常有意思、非常具体的词汇，比如跟警察、犯罪之类的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So if you are a fan of the TV show CSI or you like some of these investigation police work TV shows, this is a lesson for you.
segments.zh: 所以如果你是 CSI 这档电视节目的粉丝，或者你喜欢这类警察调查类的电视节目，那这课就是为你准备的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So why don't we go and listen to the dialogue for the first time.
segments.zh: 那我们不妨先来听第一遍对话。

segments.en: All right, Officer McGraw, give it to me straight.
segments.zh: 好了，麦格劳警官，直说吧。

segments.en: What are we looking at here?
segments.zh: 这里是什么情况？

segments.en: Detective McGee, I'm glad to see you.
segments.zh: 麦基侦探，很高兴见到你。

segments.en: We could sure use your expertise on this one.
segments.zh: 这桩案子正需要您的专业本领。

segments.en: It's a break in, but nothing seems to have been stolen.
segments.zh: 有人非法闯入，可似乎没丢什么东西。

segments.en: We received a call from the Bear family at around 1030 this morning.
segments.zh: 今天上午十点半左右，我们接到了熊一家的电话。

segments.en: They'd gone out for a walk before breakfast and came home to this mess.
segments.zh: 他们早饭前出去散步，回家就发现屋里乱成这样。

segments.en: Broken chairs and porridge all over the place.
segments.zh: 到处都是破椅子和粥。

segments.en: Apparently Mama Bear had made the porridge a little too hot, you see.
segments.zh: 显然，熊妈妈把粥煮得有点太烫了，你看。

segments.en: They were waiting for it to cool down.
segments.zh: 他们在等它凉下来。

segments.en: Okay then, let's start examining the evidence.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们开始检查证据。

segments.en: Have the forensics team been in yet?
segments.zh: 技术鉴证人员来过了吗？

segments.en: Yes sir.
segments.zh: 是的，先生。

segments.en: We found some fingerprints on the bowls and are analyzing them back at the lab as we speak.
segments.zh: 我们在碗上发现了一些指纹，并在我们说话的时候在实验室分析它们。

segments.en: Hopefully they will be able to identify the burglar soon.
segments.zh: 希望他们能够尽快识别出窃贼。

segments.en: Hmm.
segments.zh: 嗯。

segments.en: Aha!
segments.zh: 哈!

segments.en: What's this?
segments.zh: 这是什么?

segments.en: A strand of golden hair.
segments.zh: 一缕金色的头发。

segments.en: This is a very important piece of trace evidence, McGraw.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常重要的痕迹证据，麦格劳。

segments.en: It tells me the suspect has long golden hair and very few men have long golden hair.
segments.zh: 它告诉我嫌疑人有一头金色的长发，很少有男人有长长的金发。

segments.en: So our criminal could be a woman.
segments.zh: 所以我们的罪犯可能是女性。

segments.en: A woman?
segments.zh: 女人？

segments.en: Was she working alone?
segments.zh: 她是单独作案的吗？

segments.en: Did she have an accomplice?
segments.zh: 她有同谋吗？

segments.en: An accomplice?
segments.zh: 同谋？

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: No, McGraw.
segments.zh: 不，麦格劳。

segments.en: She was definitely working alone.
segments.zh: 她肯定是单独作案。

segments.en: See here, there are footprints in the porridge.
segments.zh: 看这里，粥里有脚印。

segments.en: Here on the floor, small footprints.
segments.zh: 在地板上，小脚印。

segments.en: This tells me that our suspect is small and could possibly be a child.
segments.zh: 这告诉我，我们的嫌疑人很小，可能是个孩子。

segments.en: A child?
segments.zh: 一个孩子？

segments.en: Surely not, sir.
segments.zh: 当然不是，先生。

segments.en: We must follow the clues, McGraw.
segments.zh: 我们必须遵循线索，麦格劳。

segments.en: The evidence doesn't lie.
segments.zh: 证据没有说谎。

segments.en: Now let's reconstruct the crime.
segments.zh: 现在来还原作案过程。

segments.en: The suspect came in, sat in each chair breaking the smallest one into little pieces.
segments.zh: 嫌疑人进屋后，把每把椅子都坐了一遍，还把最小的那把坐得粉碎。

segments.en: Next, the porridge.
segments.zh: 接下来，粥。

segments.en: She obviously tried to eat it and because it was so hot, she dropped it on the floor, making this mess.
segments.zh: 她显然想吃它，因为它太热了，她把它扔在了地板上，把它弄得一团糟。

segments.en: Hmm.
segments.zh: 嗯。

segments.en: Interesting.
segments.zh: 有意思。

segments.en: These footprints seem to lead upstairs.
segments.zh: 这些脚印似乎通向楼上。

segments.en: McGraw, did your officers clear the scene?
segments.zh: 麦格劳，你的警员确认现场没人了吗？

segments.en: Well, there was no one down here.
segments.zh: 好吧，这楼下一个人也没有。

segments.en: Maybe we forgot to check upstairs.
segments.zh: 也许我们忘了检查楼上。

segments.en: Hey, what's with all the noise?
segments.zh: 嘿，所有的噪音是怎么回事？

segments.en: I'm trying to sleep up here.
segments.zh: 我在楼上想睡觉呢。

segments.en: There she is.
segments.zh: 她在那里。

segments.en: Get her.
segments.zh: 抓住她！

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So a lot of interesting phrases there.
segments.zh: 所以那里有很多有趣的短语。

segments.en: They are obviously investigating a break-in.
segments.zh: 他们显然正在调查闯入事件。

segments.en: Okay a break-in, yeah.
segments.zh: 好吧，闯入，是的。

segments.en: So someone broke into this family's house.
segments.zh: 所以有人闯入了这个家庭的房子。

segments.en: So they have to investigate the evidence and some of the things that were left behind.
segments.zh: 所以他们必须调查证据和一些留下的东西。

segments.en: So now why don't we take a look on Language Takeaway, some of the specific words they used.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们为什么不看看语言要点，他们使用的一些特定词。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Alright the first word that we have is forensics, the forensics team.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们第一个词是 forensics，法医团队。

segments.en: Forensics team.
segments.zh: 法医团队。

segments.en: So a forensics team is a team at a police department or police station that studies the things that are left behind after a crime.
segments.zh: 所以法医团队是警察局里的一支队伍，专门研究犯罪后留下的东西。

segments.en: Alright so that team goes and collects the evidence.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以团队去收集证据。

segments.en: So you could look at hair or fingerprints or footprints, things like that.
segments.zh: 所以你可以看看头发、指纹或脚印，诸如此类。

segments.en: A forensics team is kind of like a team that puts together puzzle pieces trying to figure out what the story was.
segments.zh: 一个法医团队有点像一个团队，它将拼图块拼凑起来，试图弄清楚故事是什么。

segments.en: So as you said, the TV show CSI, the whole show revolves around, follows a group of forensic scientists who go to crime scenes and look at blood and different pieces of evidence that are left behind.
segments.zh: 正如你所说，那部电视剧 CSI，整部剧就是围绕、跟随一组法医科学家，他们去犯罪现场查看血液和各种留下的证据。

segments.en: Very cool.
segments.zh: 真酷。

segments.en: So one piece of evidence that a forensics team might look at is a fingerprint.
segments.zh: 因此，取证团队可能会看到的一个证据是指纹。

segments.en: That's right, a fingerprint or in the dialogue we found fingerprints, the plural form.
segments.zh: 没错，指纹，或者对话里出现的是 fingerprints，复数形式。

segments.en: Okay so for example, if you go to a police station because the police think that you have committed a crime, the police will take your fingerprints.
segments.zh: 好吧，例如，如果你因为警察认为你犯罪而去警察局，警察会取你的指纹。

segments.en: That means they'll put your finger, that means they'll put your fingers into ink and they will make you push your fingers onto a piece of paper to see what your fingers look like.
segments.zh: 这意味着他们会把你的手指，也就是把你的手指按进墨水里，然后让你把手指按到一张纸上，看看你的指纹是什么样的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So our fingerprints have a unique pattern.
segments.zh: 所以我们的指纹有独特的图案。

segments.en: Everyone has different fingerprints.
segments.zh: 每个人都有不同的指纹。

segments.en: There are no two fingerprints alike in the world, right?
segments.zh: 世界上没有两个相同的指纹，对吧？

segments.en: Right, so it's kind of like a form of identification.
segments.zh: 对，所以它有点像一种识别形式。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: That's right, so that is your fingerprint.
segments.zh: 没错，这就是你的指纹。

segments.en: So moving on, we talked about fingerprints and the scientists who are investigating the crime scene and they are talking about a very important piece of trace evidence.
segments.zh: 接下来，我们谈到了指纹，还有正在调查犯罪现场的科学家，他们谈到了一件非常重要的痕迹证据。

segments.en: Okay well let's look first at the second word there.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们先看看那里的第二个词。

segments.en: We've got the word evidence.
segments.zh: 我们有证据这个词。

segments.en: So evidence is something that is usually physical like a piece of clothing or hair that can be used against someone when we're trying to prove that they have committed a crime.
segments.zh: 因此，当我们试图证明他们犯罪时，证据通常是物理上的，可以用来对付某人。

segments.en: Right, so for example a weapon or fingerprints, all that is evidence.
segments.zh: 对，例如武器或指纹，所有这些都是证据。

segments.en: Okay so Marco, what's the difference between evidence and trace evidence?
segments.zh: 好吧，马可，证据和痕迹证据有什么区别？

segments.en: Well as you notice you have the specific word there, trace.
segments.zh: 好吧，当你注意到你有特定的词时，追踪。

segments.en: And to trace means to follow or to connect, right?
segments.zh: 追踪意味着跟随或连接，对吧？

segments.en: So what you're doing here is you're taking this evidence to follow or connect the person that committed the crime.
segments.zh: 所以你在这里所做的是你正在利用这些证据来跟踪或联系犯罪的人。

segments.en: So for example, fingerprints lets you know who committed the crime.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，指纹可以让您知道谁犯罪。

segments.en: Okay, or maybe if you have blood you can find out who did this crime.
segments.zh: 好吧，或者如果你有血，你可以找出谁犯了这个罪。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But what about like a broken window?
segments.zh: 但是像一扇破窗户呢？

segments.en: Well that's just evidence.
segments.zh: 好吧，这只是证据。

segments.en: It just lets you know how the crime was committed, maybe how they got into the house.
segments.zh: 它只是让你知道犯罪是如何发生的，也许是他们是如何进入房子的。

segments.en: But not who did it.
segments.zh: 但不是谁做的。

segments.en: But not who did it.
segments.zh: 但不是谁做的。

segments.en: Okay, so trace evidence helps you connect the crime to the person who committed the crime.
segments.zh: 好的，所以痕迹证据能帮你把犯罪和作案的人联系起来。

segments.en: And well moving on, we found that very important piece of trace evidence which was a piece of or a strand of golden hair and the police officer said, well this tells me that the suspect has long golden hair.
segments.zh: 接下来，我们发现了一件非常重要的痕迹证据，是一小撮、一缕金色的头发，警察说，这告诉我嫌疑人有一头金色的长发。

segments.en: So a suspect.
segments.zh: 所以是嫌疑人。

segments.en: Okay this word, it looks exactly the same as the word to suspect.
segments.zh: 好吧，这个词跟动词 suspect 拼写完全一样。

segments.en: But be careful because we say these two words in different ways.
segments.zh: 但要小心，因为这两个词的读法不一样。

segments.en: So to suspect, that's a verb.
segments.zh: suspect 作动词，意思是“怀疑”。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So I suspect Marco did it.
segments.zh: 所以我怀疑是马可干的。

segments.en: So that means I think or I imagine.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着我想或我想象。

segments.en: Right, whereas a suspect, a noun, a suspect is a person.
segments.zh: 对，而嫌疑人，名词，嫌疑人是人。

segments.en: So the person who we think or the person who the police think committed a crime.
segments.zh: 所以我们认为的人或警方认为犯罪的人。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So for example, we're talking about some trace evidence like long blonde hair.
segments.zh: 所以比如，我们在说的是痕迹证据，像是长长的金发。

segments.en: That means the suspect is probably a woman and is probably blonde.
segments.zh: 这意味着嫌疑人可能是女性，可能是金发女郎。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And it's interesting that you use the verb to suspect and a suspect all because you're not sure yet.
segments.zh: 有趣的是，你会用动词 suspect，也用名词 suspect，都是因为还不确定。

segments.en: So this person may have committed the crime or may not.
segments.zh: 所以这个人可能犯了罪，也可能没有。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So we have to wait until the trial.
segments.zh: 所以我们必须等到审判。

segments.en: We have to wait until we prove this person is guilty before we can say that they actually committed the crime.
segments.zh: 我们必须等到我们证明这个人有罪才能说他们真的犯了罪。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And well, you have a suspect and usually you also have somebody who is an accomplice to the crime or to the suspect.
segments.zh: 好吧，你有一个嫌疑人，通常你还有一个人是犯罪的帮凶或嫌疑人。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a suspect, as we said, is a person.
segments.zh: 正如我们所说，嫌疑人是一个人。

segments.en: It's a noun.
segments.zh: 这是个名词。

segments.en: So is an accomplice.
segments.zh: 同谋也是如此。

segments.en: So accomplice is a suspect's helper.
segments.zh: 所以同谋是嫌疑人的帮手。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So basically if you're robbing a bank and I wait outside in the car, right, while you're robbing the bank, then I am an accomplice.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，如果你在抢劫银行，我在车外等，对，当你抢银行的时候，那么我是同谋。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And under most laws, you could be sentenced to jail.
segments.zh: 根据大多数法律，您可能会被判处监禁。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So the accomplice usually doesn't commit the crime, right?
segments.zh: 所以同谋通常不会犯罪，对吧？

segments.en: You robbed the bank, but I just waited outside in the car to drive you out.
segments.zh: 你抢了银行，但我只是在车外等着开车带你离开。

segments.en: So I didn't rob the bank.
segments.zh: 所以我没有抢银行。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But sometimes accomplices do also have guns and shoot people or knives.
segments.zh: 但有时同伙也有枪、刀，也会开枪射人。

segments.en: So an accomplice is basically just the helper of the criminal, but they can get in trouble too.
segments.zh: 所以同谋基本上只是罪犯的帮助者，但他们也可能遇到麻烦。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So basically it's a person that helps out and knows about the crime, but didn't tell the police about it.
segments.zh: 所以基本上是一个帮助并知道犯罪的人，但没有告诉警方。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: That's a really important aspect.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常重要的方面。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a lot of interesting words there all related to crimes.
segments.zh: 所以很多有趣的词都与犯罪有关。

segments.en: Why don't we move on now to a couple of different phrases that we have prepared for you on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 我们不妨接着看几个我们在流利表达里为你准备的短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: I like this.
segments.zh: 我喜欢这个。

segments.en: This first phrase, it's a phrase you might hear a lot actually in police shows.
segments.zh: 第一个短语，你在警察节目里可能经常听到。

segments.en: Give it to me straight.
segments.zh: 有话直说。

segments.en: Give it to me straight.
segments.zh: 有话直说。

segments.en: Actually, also you can use it when you're just talking to someone and they're like hesitant, right?
segments.zh: 实际上，当您只是在与某人交谈并且他们犹豫不决时，您也可以使用它，对吧？

segments.en: Like, I don't know how to tell you this, but...
segments.zh: 就像，我不知道如何告诉你，但是...

segments.en: I'm not so sure.
segments.zh: 我不太确定。

segments.en: I don't think you're going to like what I have to say.
segments.zh: 我不认为你会喜欢我要说的话。

segments.en: So I can just say, okay, come on, just give it to me straight.
segments.zh: 所以我可以说，好吧，来吧，直接给我吧。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: I don't like your shirt.
segments.zh: 我不喜欢你的衬衫。

segments.en: No, I'm just kidding.
segments.zh: 没有，我只是在开玩笑。

segments.en: It's a nice shirt.
segments.zh: 这是一件不错的衬衫。

segments.en: But what you're basically asking for is the person to say, be honest with me.
segments.zh: 但你基本上要求的是那个人，对我说实话。

segments.en: Be direct.
segments.zh: 直说吧。

segments.en: Be direct.
segments.zh: 直说吧。

segments.en: Straight can mean both of those things, honest or straightforward or quick.
segments.zh: straight 可以表示这两种意思：诚实、直接，或者干脆。

segments.en: You don't want someone to go around and around and say lots of different things.
segments.zh: 你不希望有人四处走动，说很多不同的话。

segments.en: So I guess, yeah, that does make sense.
segments.zh: 所以我想，是的，这确实有道理。

segments.en: Give it to me straight maybe comes from straightforward.
segments.zh: Give it to me straight 也许来自 straightforward。

segments.en: So to be straightforward is to not hesitate to just say something directly and honestly.
segments.zh: 所以直截了当就是毫不犹豫地直接和诚实地说些什么。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So moving on to our next phrase, McGraw is talking about the bulls and he said, well, they are analyzing them back at the lab as we speak.
segments.zh: 接下来看下一个短语，麦格劳在讲那些碗，他说，好吧，就在我们说话这会儿，他们正在实验室分析它们。

segments.en: As we speak.
segments.zh: 在我们说话的时候。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is actually a phrase that refers to time.
segments.zh: 所以这实际上是一个指时间的短语。

segments.en: So in this instance, what he's basically saying is right now.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，他基本上说的是现在。

segments.en: They're being analyzed right now or in this moment.
segments.zh: 它们现在或此时正在被分析。

segments.en: So it's a way of indicating that something is happening at this very moment.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种表明在这一刻正在发生的事情的方式。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So I could say, did you know that the president is giving a speech as we speak?
segments.zh: 所以我可以说，你知道总统此刻正在发表演讲吗？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that means the president is talking right now.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着总统现在正在说话。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: As we speak.
segments.zh: 在我们说话的时候。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good phrase.
segments.zh: 这是个很好的短语。

segments.en: Now, moving on to our third phrase, Detective McGee was talking about reconstructing the crime.
segments.zh: 现在，继续我们的第三个短语，侦探麦基正在谈论重建犯罪。

segments.en: He said, let's reconstruct the crime.
segments.zh: 他说，让我们重建犯罪。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So I don't know if any of you watch these crime TV shows like Dexter or CSI.
segments.zh: 所以我不知道你们中是否有人看过这些犯罪电视节目，比如 Dexter 或 CSI。

segments.en: This is my favorite part because they tell you exactly what they believe happened.
segments.zh: 这是我最喜欢的部分，因为他们准确地告诉你他们相信发生了什么。

segments.en: So to reconstruct means to build again or to recreate, to create again.
segments.zh: 所以重建意味着重新构建或重新创建，再次创建。

segments.en: So basically they start at the beginning and they pretend to follow what happened during the crime.
segments.zh: 所以基本上他们从头开始，他们假装跟随犯罪期间发生的事情。

segments.en: So that's basically the verb to reconstruct, to rebuild, recreate.
segments.zh: 所以这就是动词 reconstruct，也就是重建、重新还原。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Reconstruct the crime.
segments.zh: 重建犯罪。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And what about our last phrase?
segments.zh: 最后一个短语是什么呢？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So our last phrase is again, a very typical police phrase.
segments.zh: 所以我们的最后一句话又是一个非常典型的警察短语。

segments.en: We hear this a lot when there's been a crime or on TV when they're talking about the scene of the crime, that means the place where the crime happened.
segments.zh: 犯罪发生的时候，或者电视上谈到犯罪现场（也就是犯罪发生的地方）时，我们经常听到这个说法。

segments.en: And the police say we need to clear the scene or did the officers clear the scene?
segments.zh: 警察会说 we need to clear the scene，或者说 did the officers clear the scene？

segments.en: So to clear means to empty out.
segments.zh: 所以 clear 的意思是清空。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But they're not talking about emptying out the evidence or removing everything from the house.
segments.zh: 但他们不是在谈论清空证据或清除房子里的所有东西。

segments.en: They're just saying to remove people, right?
segments.zh: 他们只是说要移除人，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Or obstructions.
segments.zh: 或障碍物。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So a police officer would want to make all the people go away.
segments.zh: 所以警察会想让所有人都走开。

segments.en: Well, because you don't want people stepping on the evidence or maybe putting their fingerprints all over the place.
segments.zh: 好吧，因为你不希望人们踩到证据，或者可能把他们的指纹放到各个地方。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it's very important that the officers, the police officers clear the scene so that they can start their investigation.
segments.zh: 因此，警官、警察清理现场非常重要，以便他们可以开始调查。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: A lot of interesting phrases there.
segments.zh: 那里有很多有趣的短语。

segments.en: I think we should go back.
segments.zh: 我想我们应该回去。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to the dialogue for the last time and we'll come back and talk a little bit more this.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不最后一次听对话，我们会回来多谈一点。

segments.en: And we'll come back and talk a little bit more about this really interesting topic.
segments.zh: 我们会回来再谈谈这个非常有趣的话题。

segments.en: All right, Officer McGraw, give it to me straight.
segments.zh: 好了，麦格劳警官，直说吧。

segments.en: What are we looking at here?
segments.zh: 这里是什么情况？

segments.en: Detective McGee, glad to see you.
segments.zh: 麦基侦探，很高兴见到你。

segments.en: We could sure use your expertise on this one.
segments.zh: 这桩案子正需要您的专业本领。

segments.en: It's a break in, but nothing seems to have been stolen.
segments.zh: 有人非法闯入，可似乎没丢什么东西。

segments.en: We received a call from the Bear family at around 1030 this morning.
segments.zh: 今天上午十点半左右，我们接到了熊一家的电话。

segments.en: They'd gone out for a walk before breakfast and came home to this mess.
segments.zh: 他们早饭前出去散步，回家就发现屋里乱成这样。

segments.en: Broken chairs and porridge all over the place.
segments.zh: 到处都是破椅子和粥。

segments.en: Apparently Mama Bear had made the porridge a little too hot, you see.
segments.zh: 显然，熊妈妈把粥煮得有点太烫了，你看。

segments.en: They were waiting for it to cool down.
segments.zh: 他们在等它凉下来。

segments.en: Okay, then let's start examining the evidence.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们开始检查证据。

segments.en: Have the forensics team been in yet?
segments.zh: 技术鉴证人员来过了吗？

segments.en: Yes, sir.
segments.zh: 是，先生。

segments.en: They found some fingerprints on the bowls and are analyzing them back at the lab as we speak.
segments.zh: 他们在碗上发现了一些指纹，并在我们说话的时候在实验室分析它们。

segments.en: Hopefully they will be able to identify the burglar soon.
segments.zh: 希望他们能够尽快识别出窃贼。

segments.en: Hmm.
segments.zh: 嗯。

segments.en: Aha!
segments.zh: 哈!

segments.en: What's this?
segments.zh: 这是什么?

segments.en: A strand of golden hair.
segments.zh: 一缕金色的头发。

segments.en: This is a very important piece of trace evidence, McGraw.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常重要的痕迹证据，麦格劳。

segments.en: It tells me the suspect has long golden hair, and very few men have long golden hair.
segments.zh: 它告诉我嫌疑人有一头金色的长发，很少有男人有长长的金发。

segments.en: So our criminal could be a woman.
segments.zh: 所以我们的罪犯可能是女性。

segments.en: A woman?
segments.zh: 女人？

segments.en: Was she working alone?
segments.zh: 她是单独作案的吗？

segments.en: Did she have an accomplice?
segments.zh: 她有同谋吗？

segments.en: An accomplice?
segments.zh: 同谋？

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: No, McGraw.
segments.zh: 不，麦格劳。

segments.en: She was definitely working alone.
segments.zh: 她肯定是单独作案。

segments.en: See, here there are footprints in the porridge.
segments.zh: 看，这里有脚印，就在粥里。

segments.en: Here on the floor, small footprints.
segments.zh: 在地板上，小脚印。

segments.en: This tells me that our suspect is small, and could possibly be a child.
segments.zh: 这告诉我，我们的嫌疑人很小，可能是个孩子。

segments.en: A child?
segments.zh: 一个孩子？

segments.en: Surely not, sir.
segments.zh: 当然不是，先生。

segments.en: We must follow the clues, McGraw.
segments.zh: 我们必须遵循线索，麦格劳。

segments.en: The evidence doesn't lie.
segments.zh: 证据没有说谎。

segments.en: Now let's reconstruct the crime.
segments.zh: 现在来还原作案过程。

segments.en: The suspect came in, sat in each chair breaking the smallest one into little pieces.
segments.zh: 嫌疑人进屋后，把每把椅子都坐了一遍，还把最小的那把坐得粉碎。

segments.en: Next, the porridge, she obviously tried to eat it, and because it was so hot she dropped it on the floor, making this mess.
segments.zh: 接下来，粥，她显然是想吃的，因为太热了，她把它扔在了地板上，把它弄得一团糟。

segments.en: Hmm, interesting.
segments.zh: 嗯，很有意思。

segments.en: These footprints seem to lead upstairs.
segments.zh: 这些脚印似乎通向楼上。

segments.en: McGraw, did your officers clear the scene?
segments.zh: 麦格劳，你的警员确认现场没人了吗？

segments.en: Well, there was no one down here.
segments.zh: 好吧，这楼下一个人也没有。

segments.en: Maybe we forgot to check upstairs.
segments.zh: 也许我们忘了检查楼上。

segments.en: Hey, what's with all the noise?
segments.zh: 嘿，所有的噪音是怎么回事？

segments.en: I'm trying to sleep up here.
segments.zh: 我在楼上想睡觉呢。

segments.en: There she is!
segments.zh: 她在那里！

segments.en: Get her!
segments.zh: 抓住她！

segments.en: So you mentioned a couple of different shows, such as Dexter and CSI.
segments.zh: 所以你提到了几个不同的节目，比如 Dexter 和 CSI。

segments.en: Do you watch any of these shows?
segments.zh: 你看这些节目中的任何一个吗？

segments.en: I do.
segments.zh: 我看的。

segments.en: I'm a big fan of Dexter.
segments.zh: 我是德克斯特的忠实粉丝。

segments.en: And Dexter, as you know, works at a police station in Miami.
segments.zh: 如您所知，德克斯特在迈阿密的一个警察局工作。

segments.en: His character is in forensics.
segments.zh: 他的角色是做法医的。

segments.en: He analyzes blood.
segments.zh: 他分析血液。

segments.en: Right, he's like a blood expert.
segments.zh: 没错，他就像一个血液专家。

segments.en: But it's interesting because he is actually, he commits crimes himself.
segments.zh: 但这很有趣，因为他实际上是，他自己犯罪。

segments.en: So he uses his knowledge to help him to not get caught.
segments.zh: 所以他用他的知识来帮助他不被抓住。

segments.en: Right, so he's both a criminal and he's a police officer.
segments.zh: 对，所以他既是罪犯，也是警察。

segments.en: But he's kind of like a superhero criminal, right?
segments.zh: 但他有点像超级英雄罪犯，对吧？

segments.en: Because he doesn't kill for fun or pleasure.
segments.zh: 因为他杀人不是为了好玩或快乐。

segments.en: He just takes out people who kind of deserve it, right?
segments.zh: 他只是除掉那些有点活该的人，对吧？

segments.en: Yes, but he does kind of do it for pleasure because he's obsessed.
segments.zh: 是的，但他这样做是为了快乐，因为他很着迷。

segments.en: He can't not kill.
segments.zh: 他不能不杀。

segments.en: So instead of killing good people, he decides he will only ever kill bad people.
segments.zh: 因此，他没有杀死好人，而是决定他只会杀死坏人。

segments.en: It's a really good show.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常好的节目。

segments.en: I've watched a couple of episodes and it's very, very good.
segments.zh: 我看了几集，非常非常好。

segments.en: The same as CSI.
segments.zh: 与CSI相同。

segments.en: There are a couple of different versions.
segments.zh: 有几个不同的版本。

segments.en: There's CSI Miami, New York, and Las Vegas.
segments.zh: 有CSI迈阿密、纽约和拉斯维加斯。

segments.en: But my favorite is Las Vegas.
segments.zh: 但我最喜欢的是拉斯维加斯。

segments.en: It's very, very good.
segments.zh: 它非常非常好。

segments.en: And also Law & Order.
segments.zh: 还有法律与秩序。

segments.en: I've watched a couple of episodes of Law & Order.
segments.zh: 我看过几集《法律与秩序》。

segments.en: It's pretty good.
segments.zh: 它非常好。

segments.en: Yeah, they often talk about forensics because they have both parts.
segments.zh: 是的，他们经常谈论取证，因为他们有两个部分。

segments.en: They have the police part and the law part with the lawyers who have to use the evidence in court.
segments.zh: 他们有警察部分和法律部分，律师必须在法庭上使用证据。

segments.en: Very interesting.
segments.zh: 很有意思。

segments.en: And there's also, well, forensic scientists, they take a look at the evidence.
segments.zh: 还有，好吧，法医科学家，他们看看证据。

segments.en: But I think also they examine the body back at the morgue, right?
segments.zh: 但我认为他们也在太平间检查尸体，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: They look at the body to find out what happened to the body.
segments.zh: 他们检查尸体，弄清楚尸体上发生了什么。

segments.en: This is all a part of reconstructing the crime.
segments.zh: 这都是重建犯罪的一部分。

segments.en: So this person is also sometimes called a coroner, right?
segments.zh: 所以这个人有时也被称为验尸官，对吧？

segments.en: Okay, the person who analyzes the body.
segments.zh: 好吧，也就是分析尸体的人。

segments.en: It's pretty scary though if you think about it, having to analyze a body.
segments.zh: 不过仔细想想，得去分析一具尸体，还挺吓人的。

segments.en: I think you have to be very experienced.
segments.zh: 我认为你必须非常有经验。

segments.en: It's a very interesting...
segments.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的...

segments.en: I don't even know how somebody becomes a forensic scientist, for example.
segments.zh: 比如说，我甚至都不知道一个人怎么会成为法医科学家。

segments.en: Do you study this in school?
segments.zh: 你在学校学习这个吗？

segments.en: Oh, you can go to school for it.
segments.zh: 哦，你可以去上学。

segments.en: Yeah, they have lots of forensic programs.
segments.zh: 是的，法医相关的课程有很多。

segments.en: I think I saw on Discovery Channel, they have a reality TV show about forensic students and they're actually taken to real crime scenes and then they get eliminated one by one.
segments.zh: 我想我在探索频道上看到过，他们有一个关于法医学生的真人秀节目，他们实际上被带到了真实的犯罪现场，然后他们被一一淘汰。

segments.en: I'll have to look it up.
segments.zh: 我得查一下。

segments.en: Well, I'm curious to know, have you ever heard of this before, forensic science or forensic anthropology?
segments.zh: 好吧，我很想知道，你以前听说过法医学或法医人类学吗？

segments.en: There are lots of people who study this and who do this as a job.
segments.zh: 有很多人研究这个并将其作为工作。

segments.en: And if you're not interested in that, maybe you could tell us about what kind of crime drama TV shows you like, because we certainly love them here.
segments.zh: 如果你对此不感兴趣，也许你可以告诉我们你喜欢什么样的犯罪剧电视节目，因为我们当然喜欢它们。

segments.en: Our website is EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 我们的网站是 EnglishPod.com。

segments.en: All right, we'll see everyone there.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们会在那里见到每个人。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
